title: Heterogeneous KV sharding and prefetch profiles for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Park
description: Problem: Long-context inference on Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants shows uneven KV working-set pressure across layers and variants. Single-size KV shards and global prefetch heuristics either over-allocate GPU memory (wasting capacity) or under-prefetch (causing latency spikes and OOMs). Goal: introduce model- and variant-aware heterogeneous KV sharding plus adaptive prefetch profiles to reduce peak memory by ~12-25% for long contexts while keeping p99 token latency within SLA.
background: Existing heuristics assume near-uniform residency across layers and treat all variants the same. Recent traces show: (1) larger attention heads in some Qwen variants hold denser KV footprints, (2) mistral variants exhibit concentrated hot-layer residency, and (3) llama 2-family tends to have longer tail working sets. This ticket covers profiling, model-specific shard size selection, prefetch gating, and validation on in-production workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model memory profile module that emits recommended KV shard sizes and prefetch thresholds for Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
Automated rollout that applies profiles for a subset of traffic with safe rollback and A/B metrics
Memory reduction of at least 12% on average for long-context tests (>= 16k tokens) across benchmark suite
No more than 5% regression in p50 token latency and p99 within current SLA for canary traffic
Clear observability: new telemetry shows shard occupancy, prefetch hit/miss, and per-layer eviction rate
implementation_notes: Add model metadata table: peak_kv_density_by_layer and layer_hotness_score computed from offline traces
Introduce ShardSelector component that returns heterogenous shard sizes (per-layer or per-block) given model metadata and target occupancy
PrefetchController: move from fixed prefix-based prefetch to score-driven prefetch; trigger when predicted working set surpasses soft-threshold
Fallback: if prefetch budget exhausted or OOM risk detected, fall back to conservative uniform-shard behavior and emit anomaly event
Expose a config flag runtime.features.heterogeneous_kv_sharding (default off) and an opt-in tag for canaries
benchmark_plan: Run synthetic long-context suites using our continuous-batching harness (16k, 32k token streams) on dedicated rig with Llama-70B, Mistral-22B, Qwen-34B variants. Record GPU peak allocation, p50/p95/p99 token latency, and OOM frequency. Baseline against runtime-1.19 profiles and run ablation: (1) heterogeneous sharding only, (2) prefetch only, (3) combined.
performance_targets: Avg GPU peak memory reduction >= 12%; p50 latency regression <= 5%; p99 <= SLA; OOMs reduced for high-tail workloads
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive per-layer sharding might fragment allocator and increase small-allocation overhead. Mitigation: limit shard granularity (min shard size), batch shard compaction pass during low-util windows. Risk: mispredicted prefetch increases bandwidth. Mitigation: conservative ramp and circuit-breaker on prefetch misses.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated in staging with synthetic load. 2) Canary rollout (5% traffic) for each model family with metric watch: memory_peak, p95_lat, OOM_count. 3) If canary stable for 48h, expand to 25% then 100%. 4) Automatic rollback on OOM spike or >10% p95 regression.
observability_hooks: New metrics: kv_shard_size_bytes, kv_shard_occupancy_ratio, prefetch_requests, prefetch_miss_rate, layer_evictions_per_min
Alert: prefetch_miss_rate > 0.2 for 5m or OOM_count increase > 3x baseline
test_plan: Unit tests for ShardSelector logic with synthetic model metadata
Integration tests: end-to-end inference with continuous batch harness and mock prefetch controller
Load test: run 72h soak on dedicated cluster with mixed model families and long-context streams
Chaos test: induce sudden context-length spike and verify fallback triggers
